exposure: Women with postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), women without PPH
cohort: 74 women diagnosed with primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) out of 4567 deliveries
finding: The incidence of primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) was 1.6%, with pregnancy-induced hypertension and prolonged labor identified as the most common risk factors, and uterine atony as the most common cause.
mod_finding: 75.7% of PPH cases had a normal vaginal delivery (NVD), while 24.3% had a cesarean section; the amount of blood loss also differed between NVD and cesarean deliveries.
